titulo: The simple future: The regular future

aula.objetivo: Form the simple future of regular verbs (infinitive + endings) and of the ten most common irregular ones (tendré, haré, diré, podré, pondré, saldré, vendré, sabré, querré, habré), use it for plans, predictions, and promises, and recognize the time markers that go with it.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the simple future is built from the whole infinitive — nothing gets dropped. That holds for all three groups (-ar, -er, -ir): «hablar», «comer», «vivir». STEP 2: add these endings to the infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. They're the same for all three groups. «Hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablaréis, hablarán.» STEP 3: every form carries an accent except «nosotros»: «hablaré», «hablarás», «hablará», «hablaremos», «hablaréis», «hablarán». STEP 4: the pronoun «yo» and the others are usually dropped; the ending already tells you who. STEP 5: for the nearer future, everyday speech prefers the present or «ir a + infinitive» (lesson 30): «Mañana trabajo», «Mañana voy a trabajar». The simple future sounds firmer or more formal and shows up a lot in predictions, promises, and written text. STEP 6: uses of the future: plans («El año que viene estudiaré en Granada»), predictions («Mañana lloverá»), promises («Te llamaré esta noche»), and probability about the present («Serán las cinco», meaning "it must be five o'clock"). STEP 7: the future with «si» and the present: «Si estudias, aprobarás», with the present after «si». The future never follows «si»: you don't say «si estudiarás».
blocos.comparacao: English has no built-in future tense form at all — it just drops "will" in front of the unchanged infinitive for every single person: "I will speak, you will speak, she will speak." There's no ending to memorize and no distinction by person or number. Spanish's future really is a tacked-on suffix on the full infinitive (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án), which means six different endings to learn where English gets by with one invariant word. Don't forget the accent either: without it, «hablara» is a completely different verb form, not the future.

exemplos.ru: El año que viene viviré en Valencia.
exemplos.pt: Next year I'm going to live in Valencia.

exemplos.ru: Mañana te llamaré por la noche.
La semana que viene comeremos con mis padres.
exemplos.pt: Next week we're having lunch with my parents.
I wonder where my keys are. (I'm asking myself)

erros.motivo: The future keeps the whole infinitive: hablar + ás.
After «si», use the present, never the future.

erros.errado: [misto] Yo hablaré, tú hablarás, él hablara.
erros.certo: [misto] Yo hablaré, tú hablarás, él hablará.

erros.motivo: The «nosotros» ending is «-emos» for all three groups.

blocos.enunciado: Say three plans for next week using the regular future: «Mañana trabajaré… La semana que viene estudiaré… El sábado comeré…»
Say out loud what you do every day using the present. Then say two things you did yesterday using the pretérito indefinido.
